newsitem.title: ITALY: FOCUS - Pirelli to buy back Pirelli Tyre.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Pirelli to buy back Pirelli Tyre.

text.p: Italy's Pirelli SpA offered on Tuesday to buy all the shares it does not own in its tyre unit to simplify group structure and close the door on Pirelli Tyre's poor performance on the Amsterdam stock market.

The Italian tyre and cables maker announced it was to make a public offer for all the outstanding shares and warrants it does not already own in Pirelli Tyre Holding NV which is listed on the Dutch stock exchange.

Pirelli SpA already holds 93.6 percent of the outstanding shares and 93.7 percent of the warrants of Pirelli Tyre, and is is set to offer 19.50 guilders ($10.93) per share and 0.50 guilders per warrant in cash in the public offer.

Pirelli said the offer was based on its strategy of simplifying the group's structure and concentrating the share value of its core business -- tyres and cables -- in the major holding group Pirelli SpA.

Analysts said the move had been long awaited and was a logical step in restructuring the company. It ended a sorry tale of a listing in Amsterdam just as the world tyre industry underwent serious and costly restructuring.

Pirelli listed its tyre group in 1989 after a good spell for the world tyre industry, but the early 1990s saw severe blood letting as the industry tried to cut capacity and restructure while car demand slumped in the early 1990s.
"All tyre companies went through this trauma and then saw the European car industry sales hit rockbottom in 1993," said one industrial analyst with a major investment house.
Pirelli Tyre was set up in 1989 and floated on the Amsterdam Stock Exchange that same year. Some 11 million shares were issued at 54.00 guilders each in a heavily oversubscribed issue.

But disappointing results in the years after the flotation soon put pressure on the share price, and two further rights issues made in 1993 and 1994 were at reduced prices of 10 guilders a share and 17.10 guilders to get the stock taken up.
But after losses in the early 1990s, Pirelli Tyre turned in a net profit of 41.9 million guilders in 1995 compared with a loss of 33.8 million in the previous year.

In the first half of 1996, net profit surged to 55.4 million guilders compared with a profit of 10.7 million in the same period of 1995, and the group said it expected a further improvement in the second half of 1996.

Pirelli said the full conditions of the offer would be stated in a memorandum which is expected to be published within four weeks as soon as all formal approvals have been obtained. ABN AMRO Rothschild is acting as a financial adviser to Pirelli SpA in the offer.
Earlier on Tuesday, shares in Pirelli Tyre Holding NV were suspended in Amsterdam pending the announcement. ($1=1.784 Guilder)
